The '''1966–67 season''' is '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|64th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|35th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

== Summary ==
During Autumn the team lost the [[1966 Intercontinental Cup]] against Uruguayan side [[Peñarol]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ovaciondigital.com.uy/futbol/dia-penarol-conquisto-santiago-bernabeu.html|publisher=ovaciondigital.com.uy|title=The Day Peñarol Conquered the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|language=Spanish}}</ref> being defeated the two matches of the series.<ref>{{cite web |author= Diego Antognazza |year = 2006 |url = https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/unb-penarol-56.html |title= Peñarol's series of 56 matches unbeaten in the Primera División Profesional |editor = Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation (RSSSF) |access-date = 20 June 2020}}</ref> The club won its 12th League title ever, finishing five points above runners-up [[FC Barcelona|CF Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Diario Marca|title=La flor del Real Madrid Yé-yé|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/07/07/futbol/mas_futbol/1310030818.html?a=d4b430a7096e9c1309423dd461d4cc04&t=1354897168|access-date=7 December 2019}}</ref> New arrivals were Junquera from Langreo, Zunzunegui,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/noticias/2014/08/fallece-fernando-zunzunegui|title=Fallece Fernando Zunzunegui|publisher=[[Real Madrid CF]]|date=28 August 2014|access-date=28 August 2014}}</ref> Chato Gonzalez<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diariodeavila.es/noticia.cfm/Deportes/20090606/es/dificil/encontrar/adjetivo/explicar/siento/B16EA1EF-1A64-968D-5909AE155ECFC6BA|title="Es difícil encontrar un adjetivo para explicar lo que siento"|trans-title="It is hard to find an adjective to explain what I feel"|publisher=Diario de Ávila|language=es|date=6 June 2009|accessdate=12 March 2016}}</ref> and midfielder [[Juan Ignacio Rodriguez Rodriguez|Juanito]] both from [[Rayo Vallecano]], also Rovira from [[RCD Mallorca]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/especiales/2002/02/centenario/1955.html |title=Historia del Real Madrid, 100 años uno a uno|publisher=Diario El Mundo|access-date=7 December 2019}}</ref> Left the club retiring of football were Uruguayan central defender [[José Santamaría]] and after eight campaigns Hungarian striker [[Ferenc Puskás]] too. Also, Aguero was transferred out to Granada, Isidro to Sabadell, Morollón to Valladolid, Pedro Casado to Sabadell and Pipi Suarez to Sevilla.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/realmadrid-in-ec.html|title=Real Madrid CF – All the players in European Cups|publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]]|accessdate=18 January 2020}}</ref>

In the [[1967 Copa del Generalísimo|Copa del Generalísimo]] the club was eliminated by [[Valencia CF]] in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20170630/423783734374/el-valencia-campeon-de-copa-de-1967-celebra-el-50-aniversario-del-titulo.html|title=Valencia campeón de Copa 1967|publisher=mundodeportivo.com|language=Spanish}}</ref> Meanwhile, in the [[1966–67 European Cup|European Cup]] the squad was defeated by Helenio Herrera's [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] in the quarterfinals, losing the two matches of the series (0–1 in Madrid and 0–2 in Milan).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://footballia.net/matches/real-madrid-fc-internazionale|title=Internazionale v Real Madrid|publisher=footballia.net|language=Italian}}</ref>
